transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I guess what brings me in is that my body just feels completely out of my control. Like, at first, I was pacing around my apartment all night, just making all these notes for a supper-club. But lately... I don't know, I'm just so slowed down. My sister actually pointed out that it takes me forever just to get my shoes on now. I just can't seem to move normally.
Have you been feeling down or losing interest in activities that usually bring you joy?

Yeah, I have. The stuff that usually keeps me steady... like cooking, taking food photos, music, playing pickup soccer, or even volunteering. It all just feels really flat right now. Like, I know I used to care about those things, but I just can't make myself actually feel it anymore.
Have you been feeling more fatigued or noticed a loss of energy, even when you’re not doing much physically? Like your body feels heavy or it takes a lot more effort to get through the day?

Yeah, that's exactly it. I can sleep for most of the morning, but when I finally get up, I still feel like my arms and legs are just... full of wet sand. It's a really heavy feeling. Even just doing the basics, like walking to the bus or standing there washing some dishes, it all just feels like way too much effort right now.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately?

Yeah, definitely. Um... honestly, food just tastes like cardboard lately. I don't really have an appetite at all. Some days I barely eat anything besides, like, coffee or maybe a plain tortilla. 

And my weight... yeah, my jeans have been hanging a lot looser on me. I'm definitely not trying to lose weight, it's just... I just have no desire to eat.
Have you ever experienced a period of time before this one where you felt this same kind of low mood, loss of energy, and lack of interest in things for more than two weeks?

No... I don't think so. I mean, I've had normal bad days before, but never anything like this. It's never lasted for weeks at a time where I just couldn't function or care about anything. This is the first time I've felt this low for this long.
Have you ever experienced any other times in your life, even before this, where you felt down, lost interest in things, or had trouble functioning for a period of more than two weeks?
Um, no, like I just said, I haven't. I've never felt this bad for this long before. This is definitely the first time it's been like this.
Before this current period, have you ever had an episode where you felt down, lost interest in things, or had trouble functioning that lasted for more than two weeks?
Look, doc, I feel like you're asking me the same thing over and over. Like I said, no. I haven't ever felt this way before. This is the first time it's been this bad for this long.
Have you ever experienced a period of time where you felt unusually high, excessively energetic, or so confident that it led to risky behavior or trouble functioning normally?

Yeah, there was a time like that. It was right after I got fired from my last job. Instead of being upset about it, I just felt... I don't know, weirdly unstoppable and really excited. I had all these plans. 

But the thing was, if anyone questioned what I was doing or, you know, told me I needed to slow down, I would just completely blow up at them. I'd get so angry, like they were actively trying to ruin my life.
How long did you feel that way when you felt unusually energetic or overly confident after being fired from your last job?
Um, I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. I wasn't really keeping track of the days back then. It's all a bit of a blur now, honestly... so, yeah, I don't really know exactly how long it lasted.
Can you try to estimate how long you felt that unusually energetic and overly confident way lasted after you were fired?
I really couldn't tell you. Like I said, I wasn't paying attention to the calendar. I just know it happened, but putting a number of days or weeks on it... I just can't do that. I don't remember.
Can you think back to that time after you were fired and try to estimate whether that unusually energetic and confident period lasted for a week or more?

I... I really don't know if it was a week or not. I know you're trying to figure out the timeline, but I just don't have a good sense of how long it went on. It could have been a week, maybe more, maybe less. I just don't remember it that clearly.
Can you recall if that period after you were fired—when you felt unusually energetic and confident—lasted for at least four days straight?

I know you need a specific number... but I really just don't have one to give you. Four days, a week... I honestly can't say for sure. Like I was saying, my sense of time was just completely off back then. I would really just be guessing if I told you yes or no.
Can you recall if that unusually energetic and confident period after you were fired lasted for at least four consecutive days?

Look, like I just said... I really can't tell you. I know you're asking about four days again, but my answer hasn't changed. It's all just a blur from back then. I wish I could give you a straight yes or no, but I honestly just don't know how many days in a row it was.
Can you recall if during that time after you were fired, you had a decreased need for sleep — like feeling rested after only a few hours of sleep — for at least a few days in a row?

I don't think so. Um... even though the timeline is really blurry for me, I don't remember going without sleep and feeling fine about it. I mean, I'm pretty sure I was still sleeping, or at least I didn't notice feeling totally rested after just a couple of hours. So, no, I don't think I experienced that.
Can you recall if during that time after you were fired, you felt an exaggerated sense of confidence or self-importance — like you were on top of the world or had special abilities?

Yeah, definitely. I mean, I honestly believed I was about to build the best bilingual supper club in the city. I was so sure of it. I thought investors would be stupid not to back me... even though, you know, I had just lost my job and didn't have any money lined up at all. But at the time, I just felt like I couldn't fail.
Can you recall if that unusually energetic and confident period after you were fired lasted for at least four consecutive days?

Uh... I think we just went over this, right? Like I said a minute ago, I really just don't know. I can't remember if it was exactly four days in a row or not. That whole time is just too blurry for me to give you a specific number of days.

Can you recall if that unusually energetic and confident period after you were fired included at least four consecutive days where your mood was clearly different from your usual self and stayed elevated without returning to baseline, even briefly?

Honestly, it's pretty much the same answer as before. I really just don't remember the day-to-day details like that. I know I felt completely different from my usual self, but as for it being exactly four days straight without ever coming down to normal... I just don't know. It's all too jumbled up in my head to tell you for sure.

Can you recall if during that time after you were fired, you had at least four consecutive days where your mood was clearly elevated or irritable most of the day, nearly every day, and was different from your usual self?

Look, doc, I feel like we're going in circles here. I really don't know how else to say it. I just can't remember if it was exactly four days. I know my mood was way up, and I wasn't acting like myself at all, but counting the exact days... I just don't have that timeline in my head.
Can you recall if during that unusually energetic and confident time after being fired, your mood was elevated or irritable most of the day, nearly every day, for at least four consecutive days?

I... I really don't know what else to tell you. We keep coming back to this four days thing, and I just don't have a different answer for you. 

I know I was completely wired and not acting like myself, but I wasn't tracking the days. I just can't remember exactly how long it lasted. I'm sorry, I just don't know.
